data.cultural_impact: The name Parmida, with its Persian origins, signifies a delightful, always fragrant and beautiful garden. In the rich cultural traditions of Islam and its neighboring regions, gardens have long represented a place of serenity and respite. In various Islamic poets' works, gardens are metaphors for paradise, invoking feelings of peace, tranquility, and even paradise itself.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Parmida is a reflection of the supreme beauty and wisdom of the Creator, who is the ultimate Garden'er. In Islamic teachings, Allah (God) is known as the Gardener, who cultivates and nurtures each soul, shaping and molding it to ultimately reach the eternal garden of paradise. Parmida represents this ongoing nurturing and the ultimate reward of life, connecting one's earthly journey to the realms of divine beauty and eternal peace.
